That is failure F30, and if the photo were treated as decorative it would still fail, because a non-null alt keeps it from being ignored. Read in good faith, the claim points at this defect: the alternative does not match what the image shows. The live HTML has the same img and alt, and the screenshot shows the photo.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The desktop top-menu item "Ações Afirmativas" (href="#"). It does not lead anywhere: the theme's controller.js opens its submenu on mouseover, toggles it on click (preventDefault, and sets aria-expanded on the link), and the submenu sits in the same list item (Acessibilidade, Comunidades Tradicionais, LGBTQIAPN+, Mulheres, Negros). The claim is wrong on both counts. The link has no destination to tell, and its text names the menu section it opens, a section whose links are in its own list item. So the purpose (open the "Ações Afirmativas" menu) can be determined, and the link meets 2.4.4. Using a link with href="#" as a disclosure control, with no aria-expanded until it is used, is a 4.1.2 issue, not a 2.4.4 one. The live HTML, CSS and script match the capture. The model had the list item text and misjudged it.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The header search field (input#s inside form role=search, next to a magnifying-glass submit button). Its only label is the placeholder "Busca", which is also its accessible name. 2.4.6 asks that a label describe the field's topic or purpose, and "Busca" ("Search"), with the search icon, does: users know to type a search query. So the claim that it does not say what to enter is wrong, and it asks for more than 2.4.6 requires. Relying on the placeholder alone as a visible label is an issue for 3.3.2, not 2.4.6. The live HTML is identical, and the screenshot shows "Busca" in the field.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The placeholder "Busca" in the header search field. The theme's style.css sets input[type=text] color to --cor-texto-medio (#949494), and ::placeholder inherits it (#949494 on focus as well). The field has no background of its own and sits on the white header (--cor-background: white), and its font is 14–16px at weight 400. #949494 on #ffffff is 3.03:1, below the 4.5:1 that 1.4.3 asks for normal text. The placeholder is the field's only visible label, so it is not incidental. The screenshot crop shows light-grey "Busca" on white, and the live CSS matches.

Understanding 2.4.4 does not require the destination's exact name. The desktop link with the same name has the same href, so no shared-name issue (R1). The live destination matches what Rampa read.
